# refactor: move GitHub code out of integrations into the layered owners

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to the parent issue or its siblings.

Lands after the issue that introduces `src/composition`, and builds on it. The application-API
issue lands after this one.

## What

The GitHub issue command works exactly as before. Its code sits in the same layers as the rest of
jig, and the separate integrations folder is gone.

## Why

The GitHub feature groups command handling, orchestration, rules, contracts and external
operations in one folder that depends on both the command line and the application. The rest of jig
groups code by responsibility. Organizing GitHub the same way gives it the same owners and
dependency directions as everything else.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, GitHub, files, containers, terminal, logging), `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

This issue implements one part of the design in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. That file is
in the repository; read the sections named below. Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow
the spec and say so in the PR.

## Don't undo these

- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image. The one exception:
  `jig init` saves a credential to `.jig/.env` (owner-only, git-ignored) after the operator agrees.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged unless this issue says otherwise.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.
- If you change where something lives, update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`
  and the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any guide that names a moved path. Describe current
  behavior in the present tense.

## Target

Spec section: "Redistribute GitHub functionality".

Split mixed files by responsibility; do not assign an owner from the filename alone.

| Current (`src/integrations/github/`) | Destination |
| --- | --- |
| `command.ts`: registration, schemas, terminal descriptions | `cli` |
| `implement-issue.ts`: accepted request and publication coordination | `app` |
| `github-port.ts` and the publication/store capabilities app actually needs | `ports` |
| `octokit-github.ts` | `adapters/github` |
| `repository-identity.ts`, `run-branch-publication.ts`: discovery, remote refs, push, ancestry | the Git adapters |
| `orchestration-store.ts`: receipts and leases | a persistence adapter |
| `orchestration-state.ts`: pure acceptance, receipt, lease and refusal transitions | `domain` |
| `request-snapshot.ts`, `findings-comment.ts`: content construction | the application/presentation policy that owns it, using domain data |
| `errors.ts` | owners assigned the same way as by the error-ownership rules |

- `orchestration-store.ts` imports `app/report-cleanup.ts`. Moving it unchanged would make an
  adapter depend on app. Either app owns publication lifetime through a narrow capability, or the
  adapter owns its own self-contained cleanup.
- Domain must not import the GitHub port just to get a repository identity type. Put the shared
  identity in domain and keep request/response details in the port.
- GitHub issue implementation runs a jig run through the same application code as `jig run`.
  It supplies the accepted request, run identity, required stores and publication choice. It does
  not duplicate start/resume, locking, sandbox preparation or run cleanup.
- Preserve lease renewal, recovery markers, default-branch checks, deferred publication, required
  stores, protected-path refusal, ready/draft PR selection, and idempotent comments and PRs.
- Move specs with their subjects. Delete `src/integrations` with no forwarding modules.
- Lint: remove `integrations` from `productionModules` and the `github-is-isolated` rule in
  `.dependency-cruiser.mjs`. Remove `githubOnlyInIntegration` and the related entries in
  `eslint.config.js`, and reconcile overlapping flat-config entries so a later entry does not
  silently drop a restriction. Delete the custom scanner `src/boundary.spec.ts`. Add rules that
  adapters cannot import `app`, `flow`, `steps`, `cli` or `composition`, extending the existing
  `adapters-do-not-import-flow` rule rather than duplicating it. Add a fixture showing that a new
  file under `src/integrations/` fails ownership.
- Docs: `docs/workflow-ownership.md` still lists `integrations`; update it and
  `docs/architecture.html`.

## Done when

- [ ] `src/integrations` and `src/boundary.spec.ts` no longer exist, and
      `grep -rn integrations src .dependency-cruiser.mjs eslint.config.js scripts` finds nothing
      except the fixture that proves rejection.
- [ ] GitHub behavior tests still exercise real orchestration through ports and fakes, with
      regression tests for anything the split exposed.
- [ ] The built executable's `github implement --help` works.
- [ ] The verification below passes.

## Verification

From the repository root using the pinned Node version (`volta` in `package.json`):

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

No check may start an agent on the host or publish to GitHub. In the PR, state which owner each
moved concept now belongs to and why.


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/47

Introduce only the narrow capabilities needed to remove those crossings. Prefer app-owned publication lifetime and cleanup-result precedence over copying reportCleanup into an adapter; the store capability must still support atomic claims, renewal before outward effects, ownership loss and release on every completion path. Separate workflow-path refusal policy from Git inspection while preserving exact-revision checks and guarded publication. Define the minimal GitHub dependency-injection seam now without undertaking that broader migration or adding new adapter-to-app dependencies. Remove integrations from ownership and failure-importer lists, remove transitional CLI/composition exceptions and their fixtures, and extend the existing adapters-do-not-import-flow rule to prohibit app, flow, steps, cli and composition. docs.design:
# Goal

Redistribute GitHub issue implementation into jig’s existing responsibility layers and remove `src/integrations` without forwarding modules. Preserve command behavior, shared run execution, publication safety, recovery and persisted data compatibility.

# Context

The current implementation already has the required behavior, but its ownership is mixed:

| Behavior | Current owner and implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Executable startup | `src/composition/main.ts` builds the CLI and registers the GitHub command through transitional dependency exceptions. |
| Command input and output | `integrations/github/command.ts` declares Commander options, parses input and describes outcomes. It also parses environment variables, discovers the repository and constructs Octokit. |
| Accepted request and run execution | `integrations/github/implement-issue.ts` accepts or reuses a snapshot, checks the default branch and calls `app/run-jig.ts`. It supplies the stable run ID, `merge: false`, deferred code publication and required `git-remote` storage. |
| Publication coordination | `implement-issue.ts` chooses status comments, ready PRs, draft PRs or refusals, reconciles existing publications and persists receipts. It currently imports concrete Git helpers and constructs `OrchestrationStore`. |
| Pure state | `orchestration-state.ts` owns acceptance, receipts, leases, refusal transitions and recovery identities. Its repository identity type currently comes from `github-port.ts`. |
| External capabilities | `github-port.ts` defines GitHub operations; `octokit-github.ts` implements them. Repository discovery and branch publication directly perform Git operations. |
| Persistence and publication lifetime | `orchestration-store.ts` uses `adapters/git/remote-ref.ts` for leased updates to `refs/jig/_orchestration`. It also wraps publication ownership and imports `app/report-cleanup.ts`, which prevents a straightforward move into adapters. |
| Content | `request-snapshot.ts`, `findings-comment.ts` and functions inside `implement-issue.ts` construct accepted requests, comments and PR descriptions. |
| Failure contracts | `integrations/github/errors.ts` groups API, setup, persistence, lease and use-case failures into one feature-wide module. |

The house rules require rules to live with their owners, lifecycle ordering to have one wrapper, external inputs to be parsed at their edges, expected failures to be `Result` values and external operations to sit behind ports. Tests use colocated specs, real temporary Git repositories and fakes at external boundaries. Dependency enforcement belongs in Dependency Cruiser and its existing checker and fixtures.

`docs/specs/application-boundaries.md` requires responsibility-based ownership, domain independence and shared run lifecycle execution. Its full target also includes a container-free application API. This checkout intentionally still has `app/container.ts`, `cli/app-action.ts` and `cli/with-app.ts`; their broader migration follows this issue. `src/boundary.spec.ts`, `github-is-isolated` and `githubOnlyInIntegration` are already absent.

# Chosen approach

Split mixed modules by behavior, preserving their existing protocols and observable decisions.

## Ownership and wiring

- **CLI:** Move registration, command schemas and terminal outcome descriptions into `src/cli`. Retain existing option builders, error handling and preparation order.
- **Config:** Move GitHub environment schema and token precedence into `src/config`. Preserve `GITHUB_TOKEN` before `GH_TOKEN`, existing validation and messages. Capture environment at the existing invocation edge; do not introduce environment reads in config.
- **App:** Move accepted-request orchestration, publication selection, content construction and publication lifetime into `src/app`. Continue calling `runJig` and `openRunStore`; do not reproduce their lifecycle. App receives GitHub, repository, publication and receipt-store capabilities instead of importing concrete Git functions or constructing adapters.
- **Domain:** Move shared repository identity, orchestration state and schemas, pure transitions, recovery identity rules and protected-path policy into `src/domain`. Domain imports neither ports nor app. Keep serialized state and marker formats unchanged.
- **Ports:** Define the GitHub API contract and the narrow repository-discovery, branch-inspection/publication and receipt-store capabilities actually used by app. Keep API request/response details here, separate from shared domain identity. Contracts expose neither `RemoteRef`, Octokit nor a container.
- **Adapters:** Move Octokit into `src/adapters/github`; repository discovery and branch operations into `src/adapters/git`. Put Git-ref-backed receipt and lease persistence in `src/adapters/git` as well: it is persistence implemented by Git, so no additional top-level owner is needed.
- **Composition:** Construct and supply these implementations through a narrow GitHub wiring seam. Construction remains lazy: importing the builder or requesting help must not require credentials, probe Git, open stores or start application resources.

The minimal seam can retain the existing `appAction` invocation and `App` parameter required by `runJig` during this slice. GitHub-specific dependencies are supplied explicitly from composition; CLI does not select concrete implementations. This is a documented intermediate state, not the final public application API. Do not migrate the whole container, introduce a replacement application facade or weaken adapter restrictions to accommodate it.

## Publication lifetime and persistence

Move `withPublicationOwnership` policy into an app-owned wrapper. Its caller receives only a `whileOwned` capability. The store contract supplies atomic receipt updates and lease acquisition, renewal and release, hiding tokens, clocks and remote-ref mechanics where practical. The app wrapper centralizes release in `finally` and uses the existing cleanup-result policy; callers never assemble acquire/use/release themselves.

Preserve the 15-minute lease, renewal before each outward publication effect, exclusion of competing jobs, takeover detection and release behavior. Preserve optimistic remote-ref updates, the five-attempt contention budget, no-op updates, ref/file names and persisted schemas. No new distributed-lock protocol is introduced.

A successful publication followed by release failure returns the cleanup failure. A publication failure followed by release failure retains the publication failure and reports cleanup. A work panic still triggers release and retains its original cause. Cover these paths at the app wrapper and persistence adapter boundaries.

## Publication safety and content

The Git adapter owns exact revision lookup, fetched default-branch state, merge-base and changed-path inspection, ancestry checks and leased pushes. Domain owns which paths are prohibited. The guarded publication capability invokes that policy during inspection and refuses unsafe code before pushing; moving the predicate must not leave safety as an optional caller-side check.

Preserve inspection before receipt reuse, checkpoint/head matching, fast-forward requirements, deferred publication and refusal persistence before announcement. App continues selecting ready versus draft PRs and status comments from the actual run report and saved checkpoint. Request, comment and PR content policy stays in app and uses domain data and port DTOs. Preserve recovery markers, receipt keys, snapshot reuse and all content that affects idempotent reconciliation.

## Error ownership

Replace the feature-wide error registry with definitions at their semantic owners:

| Existing condition | Destination |
| --- | --- |
| `GithubUnavailable`, `GithubRefused`, `GithubNotFound` | GitHub port: failures of the API capability. |
| `GithubSetupInvalid` | Portable GitHub setup/discovery capability contract in ports. App translates environment-schema failures into this same contract; config does not import the port. |
| `BaseBranchMismatch` | App: prerequisite of implementing an issue. |
| `OrchestrationStateInvalid` | Receipt-store port: invalid persisted state or exhausted persistence contention. |
| `PublicationInProgress` | Publication-ownership capability in ports: acquisition or renewal cannot establish ownership. |
| `RunBranchUnpublishable` | Branch-publication port: inspection or guarded publication cannot safely proceed. |

Preserve existing tags, fields, messages and classification behavior, including absence of a classification where applicable. Use narrow failure unions at each operation and aggregate only where app needs them. Do not re-export classes from a replacement registry.

Keeping `GithubSetupInvalid` as one portable setup contract avoids splitting the tag merely because validation happens at two edges. If implementation reveals genuinely different meanings that require separate classes, the spec takes precedence: distinct classes receive distinct tags, and existing tag-bearing surfaces receive explicit compatibility translation. Record any such exception in the PR rather than silently duplicating tags.

## Enforcement and documentation

Remove `integrations` from production owners, failure importers, transitional CLI/composition exceptions and ordinary fixture inventories. Keep its only reference in the requested source/config/script search within the rejected-owner fixture. Extend `adapters-do-not-import-flow` to prohibit imports of app, flow, steps, CLI and composition; retain the existing rule rather than adding overlapping rules.

Audit ESLint flat-config overlaps and combine restrictions so later entries cannot replace earlier restrictions accidentally. Keep the existing checker’s coverage of disconnected files, erased edges, cycles, resolution and production-to-spec imports. Add no source scanner.

Update the architecture map, workflow ownership inventory, CONTRIBUTING code map and current guides naming moved paths. Explain the remaining application-container transition accurately. Historical design records remain historical.

# Alternatives considered

1. **Move whole files and preserve their dependencies.** Rejected because it leaves adapter-to-app cleanup imports, app-to-adapter construction and domain-to-port identity dependencies. Directory changes alone do not establish ownership.
2. **Give the persistence adapter a self-contained publication lifetime.** Permitted by the spec, but rejected here because result precedence and reporting are already app policy. Moving the wrapper to app reuses that policy and leaves the adapter responsible for persistence and lease mechanics without copying `reportCleanup`.
3. **Complete the application API and container migration now.** Rejected because it expands this issue into the subsequent application-API work and construction decision. Explicit GitHub capability injection removes the feature’s concrete dependencies without rewriting every command’s lifecycle.

# Assumptions

- The composition prerequisite is present, as confirmed by `src/composition/main.ts` and the package executable path.
- Existing stored receipts, lease records, request snapshots and recovery markers must remain readable without migration.
- The current real-orchestration tests are the behavioral baseline; additional tests address exposed boundaries rather than restating exports or file contents.
- Preparation ordering, credential precedence and failure presentation remain observable compatibility requirements.
- This design changes no files and runs no implementation validation; the plan specifies the evidence required from implementation.

# Non-goals

- A container-free API for all application operations, moving all container construction or deciding between Awilix and factories.
- New commands, options, retry settings, publication protocols or cleanup recovery mechanisms.
- Changing cleanup failures into warnings after successful work.
- New source scanners, ownership layers, compatibility forwarding modules or generic extension frameworks.
- Live GitHub publication, host agent execution, release tags or version bumps.

# Affected areas

`src/integrations/github` and its colocated specs; `src/cli`; `src/app`; `src/domain`; `src/ports`; `src/config`; `src/adapters/github`; `src/adapters/git`; `src/composition/main.ts` and its specs; shared test helpers importing moved types; `.dependency-cruiser.mjs`; `eslint.config.js`; `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts` and the existing checker where necessary; `docs/architecture.html`; `docs/workflow-ownership.md`; `CONTRIBUTING.md`; and current documentation or tooling that names moved paths.
docs.plan:
## Step 1 — Establish compatibility and ownership contracts

Inventory all GitHub imports, exported types, error consumers, persisted formats and moved-path references. Read the applicable house rules and the spec’s GitHub, lifecycle, error and enforcement sections alongside the current implementation. Record the old-to-new ownership mapping and the bounded exception for the existing `App`/`appAction` bridge.

Identify existing tests for accepted snapshots, required remote stores, default-branch checks, leases, receipt recovery, workflow refusals, deferred publication, ready/draft PRs and idempotent comments. Use them as the baseline and identify missing boundary cases. Confirm already-absent scanner and obsolete rules; do not recreate deletion work.

## Step 2 — Extract receipt persistence and publication lifetime together

Move repository identity and pure orchestration state, schemas and transitions into domain. Define the receipt-store and publication-ownership contracts and their failures in ports. Move Git-ref persistence into adapters/git while preserving the remote ref, file contents, conflict retries and lease semantics.

Move publication lifetime to one app wrapper, removing the persistence adapter’s dependency on `app/report-cleanup.ts`. Inject the persistence capability and preserve renewal before outward effects, ownership loss and unconditional release. Move specs with their subjects and add focused coverage for successful work with failed release, failed work with failed release, panic cleanup and lease takeover. Exercise persistence using temporary Git repositories.

## Step 3 — Move GitHub orchestration and guarded publication behind ports

Move `GithubPort` and API DTOs into ports and Octokit into adapters/github. Move repository discovery and Git inspection/push operations into adapters/git behind the capabilities app actually consumes. Extract protected-path policy into domain while retaining its enforcement inside guarded inspection/publication.

Move `implementIssue`, request snapshots, findings and other publication content policy into app. Replace concrete Git imports and store construction with supplied capabilities. Keep the existing call to `runJig` with accepted text, stable run identity, `merge: false`, deferred publication and required git-remote storage. Preserve checkpoint lookup and fallback, default-branch validation, refusal-before-comment ordering and receipt/marker reconciliation.

Assign errors to their defined owners and remove the broad feature registry. Preserve tags and messages through the portable setup contract; if a semantic split is necessary, apply the spec’s unique-tag rule and explicitly translate existing exposed surfaces.

Move behavior specs alongside app, domain, ports and adapters. Retain real orchestration through fake agents and GitHub ports, and real temporary Git repositories. Verify snapshot reuse, missing required storage, exact-revision refusal, remote ancestry protection, draft/ready selection and recovery after a successful external effect whose receipt was not saved.

## Step 4 — Wire the CLI through composition without eager resources

Move GitHub command registration, input schema and outcome descriptions into cli. Move environment validation and precedence policy into config and apply it at the existing preparation edge. Route repository discovery through its port and preserve preparation failure order and existing messages.

Have composition supply lazy concrete GitHub dependencies. Keep the existing shared application bridge only where required by the later application-API migration. Remove adapter construction from the command and imports of concrete Git implementations from GitHub application behavior.

Update command and composition tests to use supplied capabilities. Verify help and imported builders do not require credentials or create application resources, and preserve option parsing, terminal descriptions and exit behavior. Move or redistribute the cross-owner failure-ownership spec to the owners it verifies without creating another global registry.

## Step 5 — Remove transitional ownership and enforce the new boundaries

Delete the emptied `src/integrations` tree without forwarding modules. Remove its owner registration, failure-importer entries and transitional CLI/composition allowances and fixtures. Confirm `src/boundary.spec.ts`, `github-is-isolated` and `githubOnlyInIntegration` remain absent.

Extend the existing `adapters-do-not-import-flow` rule to reject app, flow, steps, cli and composition. Add dependency fixtures covering the prohibited edges through type imports, re-exports, literal dynamic imports and nested paths, without relying on incidental cycles. Add a disconnected file under src/integrations to the rejected-owner fixture and remove all other integrations references from source, dependency configuration, ESLint configuration and scripts.

Audit effective ESLint restrictions on the moved files and reconcile overlapping flat-config entries. Preserve the existing dependency checker and its resolution, cycle, disconnected-source and production-to-spec checks; introduce no scanner.

## Step 6 — Update current architecture and path references

Update docs/architecture.html, including its owner table, diagrams and GitHub detail view; docs/workflow-ownership.md, including failure and test references; and CONTRIBUTING.md’s code map. Search current guides and tooling for moved paths and update affected references in place.

Describe the current layered GitHub flow and the remaining container/API transition in the present tense. Preserve historical design records as history. Prepare the PR explanation of each moved concept’s owner, why it belongs there, reusable patterns introduced and any spec-driven tag exception.

## Step 7 — Validate behavior and delivery constraints

Using the package-pinned Node 26.13.0, run the focused moved-module tests during implementation, then complete the requested verification from the repository root:

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

Run the built executable’s help path:

```sh
node dist/composition/main.js github implement --help
```

Confirm src/integrations and src/boundary.spec.ts do not exist. Run the requested reference search and verify its only match is the rejected-owner fixture:

```sh
grep -rn integrations src .dependency-cruiser.mjs eslint.config.js scripts
```

Review the final changes for persisted-state compatibility, credential secrecy, ignored scratch paths, target-worktree isolation and shared run lifecycle preservation. Verification uses fakes and temporary repositories; it must not launch an agent on the host or publish to GitHub. Report actual check results and any unavailable validation accurately. Do not create release tags or change package versions.

slices.title: refactor(github): separate receipt storage and publication lifetime
slices.description: Implements plan steps 1, 2, 6 and 7. Treat this slice as self-contained. Establish explicit ownership for durable GitHub receipts and publication leases while preserving existing behavior. Read the applicable house rules, architecture map, boundary specification and implementation; inventory imports, exported types, failure consumers, persisted formats, moved-path references and existing behavior tests. Record ownership destinations and the bounded App/appAction exception; confirm already-absent scanner and obsolete rules without recreating deletion work. Move repository identity and pure orchestration state, schemas and transitions into domain; define receipt-store and publication-ownership capabilities and failures in ports; move Git-ref persistence into adapters/git. Preserve remote refs, serialized contents, conflict retries and lease semantics. Make one app wrapper own publication lifetime, inject persistence, and remove the persistence adapter's app/report-cleanup.ts dependency. Wire existing callers to preserve renewal before outward effects, ownership-loss behavior and unconditional release. Move specs with their subjects and test successful work with failed release, failed work with failed release, panic cleanup and lease takeover using temporary Git repositories. Update affected architecture, ownership, code-map and current path references in place, preserving historical records. This slice lands first; later slices build on its contracts and may revisit shared consumers and documentation. Done when focused tests and repository lint, dependency lint, typecheck, build and format checks pass using package-pinned Node 26.13.0, with actual results reported. Use fakes and temporary repositories; never launch host agents, publish to GitHub, expose credentials, change package versions or create release tags.

slices.title: refactor(github): wire issue publication through owned capabilities
slices.description: Implements plan steps 1, 3, 4, 6 and 7. Treat this slice as self-contained and implement it after receipt-persistence-lifetime, building on its receipt and lease contracts. It lands separately because end-to-end issue implementation and CLI preparation form a distinct behavior boundary from durable storage and lease cleanup. Read applicable rules and the specification's GitHub, lifecycle, error and enforcement sections; finish the compatibility inventory for the remaining feature. translates into GithubSetupInvalid with the same message. Owner-local
specs check the tags.

Dependency-cruiser no longer lists integrations, so a reintroduced file
there fails as unowned, and the transitional composition and cli
exceptions are gone. Specs move with their subjects and add coverage for
required remote storage under a local-only config, a PR whose receipt
failed to save, origin lookup ordering, settings precedence, origin
discovery, publication content and help without credentials. The
architecture map, workflow-ownership record (with the compatibility
inventory), CONTRIBUTING and the errors rule describe the new owners.
